questions.stem: The term 'Jahiliyyah', used for the period in Arabia before Islam, means
questions.explanation: Jahiliyyah refers to the age of ignorance of divine guidance before the mission of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).

questions.stem: Which of the following was a major idol worshipped by the Quraysh and placed in the Ka'bah before Islam?
questions.explanation: Hubal was the chief idol in the Ka'bah; al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat were other well-known idols of Arabia.

questions.stem: Politically, pre-Islamic Arabia was organised mainly
options: as a single kingdom under one king
along tribal lines, each tribe led by its own chief (shaykh)
as a province ruled from Rome
as a republic with an elected parliament
questions.explanation: Arabia had no central government; loyalty was to the tribe and clan under a shaykh, which caused frequent feuds.

questions.topic: Birth and marriage of the Prophet
questions.stem: Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) was born in Makkah in the year known as
questions.explanation: He was born about 570 CE, the year Abrahah attacked Makkah with elephants.

questions.topic: Call to prophethood and his mission
questions.stem: The person who told Khadijah that the experience of the Prophet (S.A.W.) in Cave Hira was like that of Musa was
questions.explanation: Khadijah's cousin Waraqah, a learned Christian, recognised the angel as the one who had come to Musa.

questions.stem: During the Hijrah, the Prophet (S.A.W.) and Abu Bakr hid for three days in
questions.explanation: They sheltered in Cave Thawr, south of Makkah, while the Quraysh searched for them.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a direct significance of the Hijrah?
options: It ended all hostilities between the Muslims and the Quraysh
It marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar
It led to the immediate conquest of Makkah
It brought the revelation of the Qur'an to an end
questions.explanation: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar, introduced during Umar's caliphate, counts from the year of the Hijrah (622 CE).

questions.topic: Formation of the Ummah and the Madinan Constitution
questions.stem: The written agreement made by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to regulate relations among Muslims, Jews and other groups in Madinah is known as
questions.explanation: The Sahifah of Madinah set out rights and duties of the different communities in the city.

questions.topic: The Battles of Badr, Uhud and Khandaq
questions.stem: The first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraysh, in which the Muslims won despite being fewer, was the Battle of
questions.explanation: Badr (2 A.H.) was a decisive victory for about 313 Muslims over a much larger Makkan force.

questions.topic: The Battles of Badr, Uhud and Khandaq
questions.stem: The trench dug to defend Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq was suggested by
questions.explanation: Salman the Persian proposed the trench, a strategy known in Persia.

questions.topic: The Battles of Badr, Uhud and Khandaq
questions.stem: The main reason the Muslims suffered losses at the Battle of Uhud was that
options: the archers left their positions on the hill against the Prophet's instruction
the Jews of Madinah fought against them in the battle
they were attacked during the Hajj
questions.explanation: When the archers left their post to collect booty, Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacked the Muslims from behind.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a term of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
options: The Muslims were to pay tribute to the Quraysh
The Ka'bah was to be handed over to the Muslims immediately
Makkah was to become part of the Byzantine empire
The Muslims were to return to Madinah that year and perform 'Umrah the following year
questions.explanation: The treaty postponed the 'Umrah to the following year and set a ten-year truce, among other terms.

questions.stem: When Makkah was conquered in 8 A.H., the Prophet (S.A.W.)
options: executed all the leaders of the Quraysh
granted a general amnesty to the people of Makkah
made Abu Sufyan king of Arabia
questions.explanation: He forgave his former enemies and cleared the Ka'bah of idols, showing mercy in victory.

questions.stem: During the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet (S.A.W.) delivered his famous sermon at
questions.explanation: The Farewell Sermon (10 A.H.) was delivered on the plain of 'Arafat during the Hajj.

questions.stem: Which leadership quality of the Prophet (S.A.W.) is shown by his consulting his companions before the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: He practised shura, consulting his companions on important matters.

questions.stem: The first Caliph of Islam after the death of the Prophet (S.A.W.) was
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was chosen as the first Caliph in 11 A.H.

questions.stem: The Ridda wars during the caliphate of Abu Bakr were fought against
options: tribes that refused to pay Zakat or followed false prophets
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr fought the apostates and those withholding Zakat to restore the unity of Arabia.

questions.stem: The Caliph who introduced the Hijri calendar and established the diwan (public register) was
questions.explanation: 'Umar's administrative reforms included the Hijri calendar and the diwan for stipends.

questions.topic: Spread of Islam in West Africa
questions.stem: Islam first reached West Africa mainly through
questions.explanation: North African and Arab traders on the trans-Saharan routes introduced Islam peacefully.

questions.topic: Spread of Islam in West Africa
questions.stem: The al-Murabitun (Almoravids), who influenced the spread of Islam in ancient Ghana, were led in their early days by
questions.explanation: 'Abdullah ibn Yasin founded the Almoravid movement in the 11th century.

questions.topic: Impact of Islam on ancient West African empires
questions.stem: The ruler of Mali whose lavish pilgrimage to Makkah in 1324 made the empire famous in the Muslim world was
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's Hajj displayed Mali's wealth and brought scholars and architects back to Mali.

questions.topic: Impact of Islam on ancient West African empires
questions.stem: Which of the following was a linguistic impact of Islam on ancient West African empires?
options: The replacement of all local languages with Arabic
The adoption of Arabic script for record keeping and correspondence
The introduction of the Latin alphabet
questions.explanation: Arabic became the language of learning and administration, and local languages were written in Arabic script (Ajami).

questions.stem: One reason for the piecemeal revelation of the Qur'an was that
options: the angel could not carry it all at once
the Prophet asked for it to be shortened
it made memorisation and gradual application of its laws easier
the Quraysh demanded it in parts
questions.explanation: Gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet, eased memorisation and allowed laws to be introduced step by step in response to events.

questions.stem: The Companion who led the compilation of the Qur'an into one volume during the caliphate of Abu Bakr was
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit, a scribe of revelation, compiled the Qur'an after many memorisers died at Yamamah.

questions.stem: A surah revealed after the Hijrah, which often deals with laws on family, society and warfare, is classified as
questions.explanation: Madani suwar were revealed after the Hijrah and emphasise legislation; Makki suwar stress faith, Tawhid and the Hereafter.

questions.stem: Muslims regard the Qur'an mainly as
options: a history book of the Arabs
a collection of poems by the Prophet
a book of the Prophet's personal sayings
the final revealed guidance from Allah for all aspects of life
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is the word of Allah and the primary source of guidance in belief, worship, morals and law.

questions.stem: The first five verses of the Qur'an to be revealed are found in
questions.explanation: Q.96:1-5, beginning 'Iqra'', was the first revelation in Cave Hira.

questions.stem: The surah recited in every rak'ah of Salat is
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is recited in every unit (rak'ah) of prayer.

questions.stem: Suratul-Qadr describes the Night of Majesty as
options: the night of the Prophet's birth
questions.explanation: Q.97:3 states that Laylatul-Qadr is better than a thousand months.

questions.stem: The surah that tells the Prophet (S.A.W.) to say 'To you your religion and to me my religion' is
questions.explanation: Q.109 rejects compromise in worship while showing that there is no compulsion in religion.

questions.stem: Suratul-Falaq and Suratun-Nas are together called al-Mu'awwidhatayn because they
options: seek refuge in Allah from evil
tell the story of the Prophets
questions.explanation: Both begin 'Qul a'udhu' (Say: I seek refuge) and are recited for protection.

questions.stem: Suratud-Duha was revealed to comfort the Prophet (S.A.W.) when
options: he lost the Battle of Uhud
revelation had paused for a period
questions.explanation: It reassures him that his Lord had not forsaken him and reminds him of past favours, such as care when he was an orphan.

questions.stem: According to Q.17:23, a Muslim must not say to his aged parents even
questions.explanation: The verse forbids even the slightest expression of annoyance towards parents.

questions.stem: Q.61:2-3 condemns believers who
options: say what they do not do
questions.explanation: Allah strongly dislikes people saying what they do not practise, which is a lesson in honesty and integrity.

questions.stem: According to Q.2:219, in wine and gambling there is
options: no sin if done in moderation
great sin and some benefit, but the sin is greater than the benefit
questions.explanation: The verse admits some worldly benefit but declares the harm greater; Q.5:90-91 later forbids them completely.

questions.stem: The chain of narrators through whom a Hadith is transmitted is called
questions.explanation: Isnad is the chain; Matn is the text; Rawi is a narrator.

questions.stem: A Hadith whose chain is unbroken and whose narrators are upright and of perfect memory is classified as
questions.explanation: Sahih (sound) hadith meets all the conditions of authenticity; Hasan is slightly lower in the narrators' precision.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the Six Sound Collections (as-Sihah as-Sittah)?
questions.explanation: The six are al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

questions.stem: The main difference between Hadith and Sunnah is that
options: Hadith is the report or narration, while Sunnah is the practice or way of life of the Prophet (S.A.W.) that is reported
Hadith is the word of Allah, while Sunnah is the word of angels
Sunnah is found only in the Qur'an
Hadith refers only to the Prophet's actions, never to his sayings
questions.explanation: Hadith is the narrated report (sayings, acts and approvals); Sunnah is the normative practice it records.

questions.stem: The first Hadith in an-Nawawi's collection teaches that
options: paradise lies under the feet of mothers
the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Hadith 1, narrated by 'Umar, states that deeds are rewarded according to intentions.

questions.stem: According to Hadith 13 of an-Nawawi's collection, none of you truly believes until he
options: loves for his brother what he loves for himself
questions.explanation: The Hadith, narrated by Anas, teaches brotherhood and selflessness.

questions.stem: The advice repeated several times by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to a man who asked for counsel in Hadith 16 of an-Nawawi's collection was
questions.explanation: The Prophet repeated 'Do not become angry', showing the importance of self-control.

questions.stem: Hadith 34 of an-Nawawi's collection teaches that whoever sees an evil should change it with his hand; if he cannot, then
options: with his tongue, and if he cannot, then with his heart, which is the weakest of faith
he should report it only to the ruler
he should leave the town immediately
questions.explanation: The Hadith sets out stages of correcting wrong according to ability.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the articles of faith (Arkanul-Iman)?
questions.explanation: Zakat, Hajj and fasting are pillars of Islam; belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman.

questions.stem: The verse of the Qur'an known as Ayatul-Kursi is
questions.explanation: Ayatul-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne) is Q.2:255, describing Allah's majesty.

questions.stem: Suratul-Ikhlas rejects the doctrine of the Trinity by declaring that Allah
options: has a son who shares his power
questions.explanation: Q.112:3 affirms that Allah has no offspring and no parent, a basis of Tawhid.

questions.stem: According to Q.82:10-12, the angels appointed over every person
options: guard the gates of paradise only
questions.explanation: Honourable recorders (Kiraman Katibin) write down human deeds.

questions.stem: The divine book revealed to Prophet Musa (A.S.) is
questions.explanation: Tawrah to Musa, Zabur to Dawud, Injil to 'Isa and the Qur'an to Muhammad (S.A.W.).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the Ulul-'Azm (Prophets of strong will)?
questions.explanation: The Ulul-'Azm are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and Muhammad (S.A.W.).

questions.topic: The Day of Resurrection, Judgement and Eternal Life
questions.stem: The angel who will blow the trumpet to announce the Day of Resurrection is
questions.explanation: Israfil is traditionally identified as the angel of the trumpet.

questions.stem: According to Q.3:145, no soul can die except
options: at the time the person decides
by Allah's leave, at a term appointed
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that the time of death is fixed by Allah's decree, part of belief in Qada' and Qadar.

questions.stem: According to Q.4:48, Allah does not forgive
options: forgetting a verse of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Shirk, if one dies upon it, is the sin Allah does not forgive; He forgives other sins as He wills.

questions.stem: Islam condemns ancestor-worship mainly because
options: it involves praying for the dead
it directs worship meant only for Allah to created beings
it is practised only in Africa
questions.explanation: Prayer for the dead is allowed; worship of the dead, or seeking from them what only Allah gives, is shirk.

questions.stem: Taharah in Islam means
options: purification of the body, clothes and place
questions.explanation: Taharah is ritual and physical cleanliness, a precondition for Salat.

questions.stem: Which of the following nullifies Wudu'?
questions.explanation: Anything that exits from the private parts, including wind, breaks ablution.

questions.stem: Tayammum is performed when
options: a person is too busy to wash
water is unavailable or its use would cause harm
it is the month of Ramadan
questions.explanation: Tayammum with clean earth replaces Wudu' or Ghusl when water cannot be found or used (Q.5:6).

questions.stem: Which of the following makes Ghusl (ritual bath) compulsory?
questions.explanation: Ghusl is obligatory after sexual intercourse, seminal discharge, menstruation and post-natal bleeding.

questions.stem: The total number of compulsory rak'ahs in the five daily prayers is
questions.explanation: Subh 2 + Zuhr 4 + 'Asr 4 + Maghrib 3 + 'Isha' 4 = 17.

questions.stem: Sujudus-Sahwi in Salat is
options: two prostrations made to correct an error of forgetfulness in prayer
a prayer said at a funeral
the prostration made during the recitation of the Qur'an only
questions.explanation: Prostration of forgetfulness compensates for an addition or omission in Salat.

questions.stem: Salatul-Janazah differs from other prayers in that it
options: is performed only in the night
questions.explanation: The funeral prayer is performed standing with four takbirs.

questions.stem: A traveller who shortens his prayers (Qasr) reduces
options: the four-rak'ah prayers to two rak'ahs each
all prayers to one rak'ah each
questions.explanation: Only Zuhr, 'Asr and 'Isha' are shortened; Maghrib and Subh remain unchanged.

questions.stem: Fasting on the tenth day of Muharram is called the fast of
questions.explanation: 'Ashura' is the 10th of Muharram; Tasu'a is the 9th.

questions.stem: Which of the following persons is permitted not to fast in Ramadan but must make up the days later?
options: A traveller on a long journey
questions.explanation: Travellers and the temporarily sick may break the fast and repay the days (Q.2:184).

questions.stem: A person who deliberately breaks a Ramadan fast by eating without a valid excuse must, as Kaffarah, among other options
questions.explanation: The expiation is freeing a slave, fasting sixty consecutive days, or feeding sixty poor people.

questions.stem: The main difference between Zakat and Sadaqah is that
options: Sadaqah is compulsory while Zakat is voluntary
Zakat is paid only in Ramadan
Zakat is compulsory while Sadaqah is voluntary
Sadaqah can be given only to Muslims
questions.explanation: Zakat is an obligatory pillar with fixed rates; Sadaqah is voluntary charity.

questions.topic: Articles on which Zakat is paid
questions.stem: The rate of Zakat on money that has reached the nisab and been held for one lunar year is
questions.explanation: Zakat on cash, gold and silver is one-fortieth (2.5%).

questions.stem: According to Q.9:60, which of the following is among the beneficiaries of Zakat?
questions.explanation: The eight categories include the poor, the needy, collectors, debtors, wayfarers and others named in Q.9:60.

questions.stem: Zakatul-Fitr should be paid
options: on the first day of Ramadan only
at the end of the lunar year
questions.explanation: It should be given before the 'Id prayer so the poor can celebrate.

questions.topic: Pre-requisites to the performance of Hajj
questions.stem: Hajj is compulsory once in a lifetime on every Muslim who
options: is adult, sane and able to afford the journey
questions.explanation: Ability (istita'ah) is a key condition, along with Islam, puberty and sanity (Q.3:97).

questions.stem: The standing on the plain of 'Arafat during Hajj takes place on
questions.explanation: Wuquf at 'Arafat on 9 Dhul-Hijjah is the essential pillar of Hajj.

questions.stem: The type of Hajj in which the pilgrim performs 'Umrah, leaves the state of Ihram and later enters Ihram again for Hajj is
questions.explanation: Tamattu' combines 'Umrah and Hajj with a break; Qiran combines them in one Ihram; Ifrad is Hajj alone.

questions.topic: Definition and Origin of Hajj and 'Umrah
questions.stem: The rite of Sa'y between Safa and Marwah commemorates
options: Hajar's search for water for her son Isma'il
the building of the Prophet's mosque
questions.explanation: Sa'y re-enacts Hajar running between the two hills before the spring of Zamzam appeared.

questions.stem: The two primary sources of Shari'ah are
questions.explanation: Qur'an and Sunnah are primary; Ijma' and Qiyas are secondary.

questions.stem: Deriving a ruling that cocaine is forbidden from the Qur'anic prohibition of wine, because both intoxicate, is an example of
questions.explanation: Qiyas is analogical deduction based on a shared effective cause ('illah), here intoxication.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a condition for the validity of Nikah in Islam?
options: The payment or promise of Mahr (dowry) to the bride
The presence of a musical band
The building of a new house
The approval of the local government
questions.explanation: Valid Nikah requires the consent of both parties, a wali, witnesses and Mahr given to the bride (Q.4:4).

questions.stem: According to Q.4:23, a Muslim man is forbidden to marry
options: a divorced woman who has completed her 'Iddah
questions.explanation: Foster (milk) relationships forbid marriage like blood relationships; cousins and widows are lawful.

questions.topic: Rights and duties of husband and wife
questions.stem: Which of the following is a right of the wife over her husband in Islam?
options: Obedience of the husband in all matters
Control of his inheritance during his lifetime
questions.explanation: The husband must provide food, clothing and shelter for his wife (Q.65:6).

questions.stem: According to a Hadith reported by Abu Dawud, of all lawful things the most hateful to Allah is
questions.explanation: Divorce is lawful but disliked, so reconciliation should be attempted first (Q.4:35).

questions.stem: A divorce initiated by the wife in which she returns her Mahr to the husband is called
questions.explanation: In Khul' the wife buys her release; Faskh is annulment by a judge; Zihar and Li'an arise from the husband's statements.

questions.stem: The 'Iddah of a divorced woman who still menstruates is
questions.explanation: Q.2:228 sets three quru'; four months and ten days is the 'Iddah of a widow (Q.2:234).

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the social and religious life of the Arabs during the Jahiliyyah period. [12 marks]
(b) Explain five reforms introduced by Islam to correct the practices of the Jahiliyyah. [10 marks]
(c) State the location of Arabia. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Unlimited polygamy and easy divorce; women had few rights and were often inherited like property
2 marks: (a) Female infanticide: some girls were buried alive
2 marks: (a) Widespread drinking of wine, gambling, usury and tribal feuds
2 marks: (a) Idol worship: the Ka'bah housed many idols such as Hubal
2 marks: (a) Worship of al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; belief in jinn, soothsaying and divining arrows
2 marks: (a) A few Hanifs worshipped one God; some Jews and Christians lived in Arabia
2 marks: (b) Abolished idol worship and established Tawhid
2 marks: (b) Forbade female infanticide and gave women rights to inheritance and Mahr
2 marks: (b) Limited polygamy to four wives with justice
2 marks: (b) Prohibited wine, gambling and usury
2 marks: (b) Replaced tribal loyalty with brotherhood of the Ummah
3 marks: (c) Arabia is a peninsula in south-west Asia, bounded by the Red Sea to the west, the Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean to the south and the Persian (Arabian) Gulf to the east
questions.explanation: Jahiliyyah Arabia practised idolatry, infanticide, unlimited polygamy, wine-drinking, gambling and tribal warfare. Islam replaced these with Tawhid, women's rights, regulated marriage, prohibition of intoxicants, gambling and usury, and the brotherhood of believers. Arabia is a peninsula in south-west Asia between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four causes of the Hijrah of the Prophet (S.A.W.) from Makkah to Madinah. [8 marks]
(b) Describe the journey of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and Abu Bakr to Madinah. [9 marks]
(c) State four significances of the Hijrah. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Intense persecution of Muslims by the Quraysh
2 marks: (a) Death of Abu Talib and Khadijah, which removed his protection and support
2 marks: (a) The pledges of 'Aqabah, in which people of Yathrib invited and promised to protect him
2 marks: (a) The plot by the Quraysh to kill the Prophet
3 marks: (b) 'Ali slept in the Prophet's bed while he left secretly at night with Abu Bakr
3 marks: (b) They hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days while the Quraysh searched for them
3 marks: (b) They travelled by an unusual route, stopped at Quba' where he built a mosque, then entered Madinah where he was warmly received
2 marks: (c) It marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar
2 marks: (c) It led to the establishment of the first Islamic state in Madinah
2 marks: (c) It brought brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar
2 marks: (c) It gave Muslims freedom of worship and allowed Islam to spread
questions.explanation: Persecution, the loss of his protectors, the invitation and pledges of 'Aqabah and the Quraysh plot to kill him led to the Hijrah. Leaving 'Ali in his bed, he and Abu Bakr hid in Cave Thawr, then travelled to Quba' and Madinah. The Hijrah began the Islamic calendar, founded the Muslim state, united Muhajirun and Ansar and secured freedom of worship.

questions.stem:
(a) Give a brief account of the life of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab before he became Caliph. [8 marks]
(b) Discuss five contributions of 'Umar to the development of Islam during his caliphate. [15 marks]
(c) State one lesson from his life. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) He was born into the 'Adi clan of the Quraysh in Makkah and was known for his strength and courage
2 marks: (a) He initially opposed Islam strongly
2 marks: (a) He accepted Islam after hearing verses of Suratu Ta-Ha at his sister's house; Muslims then prayed openly at the Ka'bah
2 marks: (a) He became a close adviser of the Prophet, was given the title al-Faruq, and was nominated by Abu Bakr as Caliph
3 marks: (b) He introduced the Hijri calendar
3 marks: (b) He established the diwan (public register) and the bayt al-mal for stipends
3 marks: (b) He expanded the Islamic state to Syria, Iraq, Persia and Egypt
3 marks: (b) He organised administration into provinces with governors and appointed judges (qadis)
3 marks: (b) He encouraged congregational Tarawih prayers and suggested the compilation of the Qur'an to Abu Bakr
2 marks: (c) Justice, simplicity and accountability in leadership
questions.explanation: 'Umar, a strong Qurayshi who first opposed Islam, embraced it and became al-Faruq. As Caliph he introduced the Hijri calendar, the diwan and bayt al-mal, expanded and organised the state, appointed judges and promoted congregational Tarawih; his life teaches justice and simplicity.

questions.topic: Spread of Islam in West Africa
questions.stem:
(a) Discuss the roles of each of the following in the spread of Islam in West Africa: (i) traders; (ii) teachers and scholars; (iii) the Murabitun; (iv) the Sufi orders. [16 marks]
(b) Assess three ways in which Islam affected the political life of the ancient empire of Mali or Songhai. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a)(i) North African Muslim traders crossing the Sahara settled in commercial towns, married locally and won converts by example
4 marks: (a)(ii) Teachers and scholars set up Qur'anic schools, served as advisers and scribes at royal courts and spread literacy in Arabic
4 marks: (a)(iii) The Almoravids under 'Abdullah ibn Yasin preached reform and their influence weakened ancient Ghana and spread Islam among its people
4 marks: (a)(iv) Sufi orders such as the Qadiriyyah and Tijaniyyah spread Islam through zawiyas, discipleship and reform movements
3 marks: (b) Rulers such as Mansa Musa and Askia Muhammad adopted Islam, and Shari'ah influenced administration and justice
3 marks: (b) Muslim scholars served as advisers, judges and secretaries in government
3 marks: (b) Diplomatic ties were made with Muslim states of North Africa and the Middle East, aided by pilgrimages
questions.explanation: Traders, scholars, the Almoravids and Sufi orders spread Islam peacefully and through reform. In Mali and Songhai Muslim rulers applied Shari'ah, employed literate scholars in government and forged ties with the Muslim world through pilgrimage and diplomacy.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the compilation of the Qur'an during the caliphate of Abu Bakr. [10 marks]
(b) Explain the steps taken by 'Uthman ibn 'Affan to standardise the Qur'an. [10 marks]
(c) State five differences between Makki and Madani suwar. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Many memorisers (huffaz) were killed at the Battle of Yamamah
2 marks: (a) 'Umar advised Abu Bakr to compile the Qur'an to prevent its loss
2 marks: (a) Zayd ibn Thabit was appointed to collect the Qur'an from written materials and memories
2 marks: (a) He accepted only verses supported by reliable witnesses and written records
2 marks: (a) The compiled copy (suhuf) was kept by Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then Hafsah
2 marks: (b) Differences in recitation arose among Muslims in the new provinces
2 marks: (b) Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported this to 'Uthman
2 marks: (b) 'Uthman set up a committee led by Zayd ibn Thabit using Hafsah's copy
2 marks: (b) Copies were written in the dialect of the Quraysh
2 marks: (b) Copies were sent to major provinces and other copies were destroyed
1 mark: (c) Makki revealed before Hijrah; Madani after
1 mark: (c) Makki mostly short verses and suwar; Madani mostly longer
1 mark: (c) Makki stress Tawhid and the Hereafter; Madani stress laws and social life
1 mark: (c) Makki often address 'O mankind'; Madani often 'O you who believe'
1 mark: (c) Madani deal with hypocrites, People of the Book and rules of warfare
questions.explanation: After the deaths at Yamamah, Abu Bakr on 'Umar's advice had Zayd ibn Thabit compile the Qur'an into suhuf kept later by Hafsah. When recitation differences arose, 'Uthman had a committee copy the text in the Quraysh dialect and send standard copies to the provinces. Makki suwar are earlier, shorter and doctrinal; Madani suwar are later, longer and legislative.

questions.stem:
(a) Define Hadith and Sunnah. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the three parts of a Hadith. [6 marks]
(c) Name the six sound collections of Hadith and their compilers. [12 marks]
(d) State three importances of Hadith. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Hadith is a report of the sayings, actions and tacit approvals of the Prophet (S.A.W.)
2 marks: (a) Sunnah is the practice or way of life of the Prophet (S.A.W.)
2 marks: (b) Isnad: the chain of narrators
2 marks: (b) Matn: the text or content of the Hadith
2 marks: (b) Rawi: the narrator who transmits the Hadith
2 marks: (c) Sahih al-Bukhari, by Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari
2 marks: (c) Sahih Muslim, by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
2 marks: (c) Sunan Abi Dawud, by Abu Dawud as-Sijistani
2 marks: (c) Jami' at-Tirmidhi, by Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi
2 marks: (c) Sunan an-Nasa'i, by Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb an-Nasa'i
2 marks: (c) Sunan Ibn Majah, by Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah
1 mark: (d) It explains and details the Qur'an
1 mark: (d) It is the second source of Shari'ah
1 mark: (d) It provides a practical model of conduct for Muslims
questions.explanation: Hadith reports the Prophet's words, deeds and approvals; Sunnah is his practice. A Hadith has Isnad, Matn and a Rawi. The six collections are by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. Hadith explains the Qur'an, is the second source of law and models conduct.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of Kalimatush-Shahadah. [5 marks]
(b) Discuss the Islamic belief in the Oneness of Allah (Tawhid) with reference to Suratul-Ikhlas. [10 marks]
(c) Explain the Islamic position on the concept of the Trinity. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) It is the testimony 'There is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'
2 marks: (a) It is the first pillar of Islam and the declaration by which a person enters Islam
2 marks: (b) Allah is One (Ahad), unique in His essence
2 marks: (b) Allah is as-Samad: eternal, self-sufficient, on whom all depend
2 marks: (b) He neither begets nor is begotten
2 marks: (b) There is none comparable or equal to Him
2 marks: (b) Tawhid requires worship of Allah alone and rejection of shirk
3 marks: (c) Islam rejects the Trinity and holds that Allah is one without partner (Q.4:171; 5:73)
3 marks: (c) 'Isa (A.S.) is regarded as an honoured prophet and servant of Allah, not the son of God (Q.5:75)
2 marks: (c) It is unfitting for the Most Merciful to take a son (Q.19:92-93)
2 marks: (c) Attributing a son or partners to Allah is shirk
questions.explanation: The Shahadah testifies to Allah's oneness and Muhammad's messengership. Suratul-Ikhlas defines Tawhid: Allah is One, eternal and self-sufficient, neither begetting nor begotten, with none equal to Him. Islam therefore rejects the Trinity and regards 'Isa as a prophet and servant of Allah.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning and importance of Salat. [6 marks]
(b) List the five daily obligatory prayers and the number of rak'ahs in each. [10 marks]
(c) State three acts that vitiate Salat. [6 marks]
(d) What is Sujudus-Sahwi? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Salat is the prescribed ritual prayer offered five times daily; the second pillar of Islam
2 marks: (a) It brings the worshipper close to Allah and keeps him away from indecency and evil
2 marks: (a) It promotes discipline, punctuality, cleanliness and unity in congregation
2 marks: (b) Subh/Fajr: 2 rak'ahs
2 marks: (b) Zuhr: 4 rak'ahs
2 marks: (b) 'Asr: 4 rak'ahs
2 marks: (b) Maghrib: 3 rak'ahs
2 marks: (b) 'Isha': 4 rak'ahs
2 marks: (c) Talking deliberately during Salat
2 marks: (c) Eating or drinking during Salat
2 marks: (c) Loss of Wudu' (e.g. passing wind) or deliberate omission of a pillar
3 marks: (d) Two prostrations of forgetfulness made at the end of Salat to make up for an addition or omission made by mistake
questions.explanation: Salat, the second pillar, links the believer to Allah and builds discipline and unity. Subh 2, Zuhr 4, 'Asr 4, Maghrib 3 and 'Isha' 4 rak'ahs. Talking, eating or losing Wudu' invalidates it; Sujudus-Sahwi corrects forgetful errors.

questions.topic: Articles on which Zakat is paid
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Zakat and Sadaqah. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the nisab and rate of Zakat on (i) money; (ii) agricultural produce; (iii) sheep and goats. [9 marks]
(c) Name the eight categories of beneficiaries of Zakat according to Q.9:60. [8 marks]
(d) State two socio-economic benefits of Zakat. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Zakat is compulsory, with fixed rates, nisab and recipients
2 marks: (a) Sadaqah is voluntary charity given at any time, in any amount
3 marks: (b)(i) Money equal in value to the nisab of gold (about 85 g) held for one lunar year: 2.5 per cent
3 marks: (b)(ii) Crops: 10 per cent if watered by rain, 5 per cent if irrigated at cost
3 marks: (b)(iii) From 40 sheep/goats: one sheep, up to 120
1 mark: (c) The poor (al-fuqara')
1 mark: (c) The needy (al-masakin)
1 mark: (c) Those employed to collect Zakat
1 mark: (c) Those whose hearts are to be reconciled
1 mark: (c) For freeing captives/slaves
1 mark: (c) Debtors
1 mark: (c) In the cause of Allah
1 mark: (c) The wayfarer (ibnus-sabil)
2 marks: (d) It reduces poverty and narrows the gap between rich and poor
2 marks: (d) It circulates wealth and discourages hoarding
questions.explanation: Zakat is an obligatory levy; Sadaqah is voluntary. Money at nisab held a lunar year pays 2.5%, rain-fed crops 10% (irrigated 5%), and 40-120 sheep or goats one sheep. Q.9:60 names the poor, needy, collectors, those whose hearts are reconciled, captives, debtors, the cause of Allah and wayfarers. Zakat reduces poverty and circulates wealth.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain Islam's attitude to divorce. [5 marks]
(b) Explain the following kinds of divorce: (i) Talaq; (ii) Khul'; (iii) Zihar; (iv) Li'an. [12 marks]
(c) State the 'Iddah for (i) a divorced woman who menstruates; (ii) a pregnant woman; (iii) a widow; and give one purpose of 'Iddah. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Divorce is lawful but the most hateful of lawful things to Allah (Hadith in Abu Dawud)
2 marks: (a) Arbitration by representatives of both families should be attempted first (Q.4:35)
3 marks: (b)(i) Talaq: divorce pronounced by the husband; the first two are revocable within 'Iddah, the third is final
3 marks: (b)(ii) Khul': divorce sought by the wife, who returns the Mahr or gives compensation
3 marks: (b)(iii) Zihar: the husband likens his wife to his mother's back; he must perform expiation before resuming relations
3 marks: (b)(iv) Li'an: mutual oaths of imprecation when a husband accuses his wife of adultery without witnesses, after which they are separated permanently
2 marks: (c)(i) Three menstrual courses (Q.2:228)
2 marks: (c)(ii) Until she delivers (Q.65:4)
2 marks: (c)(iii) Four months and ten days (Q.2:234)
2 marks: (c) Purpose: to establish whether she is pregnant and to allow time for reconciliation
questions.explanation: Divorce is permitted but disliked; reconciliation through arbiters comes first. Talaq is by the husband, Khul' by the wife with compensation, Zihar is likening the wife to one's mother, and Li'an is mutual imprecation over an unproven adultery charge. 'Iddah is three courses, until delivery for the pregnant, and four months ten days for a widow, to confirm pregnancy status and allow reconciliation.
